$comment: THE CLASSIFICATION. An expiring signed URL is NOT a defect — it is the correct,
intended mechanism in many places. The defect is the MISMATCH between a URL's
lifetime and its consumer's contract. Every entry below is a column where a
stored signed URL is CORRECT, with the reason and the reading code path that
makes it correct. A hit in any column NOT listed here is a new mismatch and the
Adding an entry here is a judgement, not a silencer. Write the real reason.
If you cannot name the consumer and why expiry is fine for it, it is not
THE VISIBILITY-FLIP CRITERION (sharper than 'it expires later'): flipping a file
to public MOVES the S3 object, which invalidates every signed URL already handed
out for it. So the broken write pattern is: generate private -> store the signed
URL -> later flip that file public -> every stored URL dies INSTANTLY. Such a row
is already broken even when the stored URL looks fresh and its expiry is far away.
When classifying a writer, ask not only 'does this expire before the reader needs
it' but 'does anything later change this file's visibility'. The fix is to persist
PUBLIC AT GENERATION (aidream matrx_ai.media.public_media_scope()), never to flip

mitigated.reason: Stores our own expiring URLs inside message bodies, but EVERY reading path re-mints: markdown images through ImageBlock -> useRemintableSrc -> recognizeOurFileUrl, and media blocks through buildMediaSource, which recovers the file_id from the URL and hands the handler a durable file_id source. No user-visible break. NOT auto-healed because message bodies are the conversation record — rewriting them edits what was said, which is Arman's call, not an agent's.

mitigated.reason: HEALED 2026-08-11, on Arman's decision (the two images were test data he placed himself). The two recoverable files were flipped to public via the canonical primitive (aidream flip_file_to_public, the same one the heal drain uses) and 20 dead signed URLs across 7 Draft notes were rewritten to their durable cdn.matrxserver.com URLs — non-URL text byte-identical, verified by diff before applying. Both CDN URLs fetch 200 anonymously. The anon-share mismatch is CLOSED: nothing an anonymous share recipient could be shown is expiring any more. RESIDUAL, and it is not fixable: (a) one reference to file_id da5868b9-0925-47af-b6e5-f150628b8bf6, which has NO files.files row — the file is gone, so there is no identity to re-mint from and no decision can heal it; (b) verbatim third-party signed URLs pasted into note bodies, which are data, not our media. The column therefore still reports hits and always will. That is accurate, not a to-do.
